result: The behaviorMate system is an open-source, modular behavioral control platform using networked hardware and software components that communicate via UDP/JSON protocols on a LAN. The system includes a Java-based UI, Arduino-based controllers for behavior and position tracking, and VRMate software for VR display rendering using Unity. The architecture is designed to be flexible, scalable, cost-effective, and accessible without requiring users to write code.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm the system's functionality and design, noting it is 'thoroughly tested,' 'well-developed,' and provides 'compelling evidence of functionality and applicability.' One reviewer highlights the 'innovative approaches' including 'decentralized, Android-based display devices' and the 'Intranet of things scheme.' The modular architecture and ease of use are praised as 'highly desirable' features.

result: The behaviorMate system is cost-effective, with a VR rig costing approximately $3700 and a treadmill system around $1700, significantly cheaper than proprietary commercial alternatives like National Instruments systems.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognize the cost-effectiveness as a major advantage. One reviewer states 'the cost-effectiveness of the system provided' as a key strength, and another notes it creates 'an invaluable resource for neuroscience researcher looking to set up a budget-friendly VR and head-fixed imaging rig.'

result: Benchmark tests demonstrate high-fidelity, real-time performance: mean lap time error of 0.102 seconds, position error of 13 mm (max 23 mm) for treadmill, VR latency of 0.067 seconds (below mouse reaction time of ~0.1 s), and VR position tracking error of 4.1 mm.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm the benchmarking results, stating the authors 'report benchmark tests for high-fidelity, real-time update speed between the animal's movement and the behavioral control' and provide 'compelling evidence of the functionality' of the system. The quantitative performance data is accepted without critique.

result: Two-photon calcium imaging in CA1 revealed place cells in both VR and treadmill environments. VR had significantly fewer place cells (34.9%) than treadmill (44.9%). Place cells tiled the entire track in both conditions. Environment significantly affected sensitivity and specificity (higher in TM), but not amplitude, frequency, or spatial information. The differences may result from absence of tactile cues in VR.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm these findings, noting the authors 'nicely demonstrate and quantify reliable hippocampal place cell coding in both setups' and that 'this place cell characterization also provides a concrete comparison between the place cell properties observed in treadmill-based navigation vs. visual VR in a single study, which itself is a valuable contribution to the field.' The statistical analyses and interpretations are accepted without challenge.

result: Place cells exhibited remapping when exposed to novel contexts in both VR and treadmill environments. Bayesian decoding showed significantly below-chance error for familiar contexts but chance-level error for novel contexts, demonstrating context-dependent spatial coding in both systems.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings as part of the demonstration of 'reliable hippocampal place cell coding' and do not raise concerns about the remapping analysis or decoding results. The findings are treated as supporting evidence for the system's validity.

result: The behaviorMate system has been successfully used in numerous published studies for diverse experimental paradigms including head-fixed navigation with 2-photon imaging, trace fear conditioning, goal-oriented learning, optogenetic stimulation, and investigation of synaptic plasticity mechanisms. The current validation used six mice (balanced for sex) with jGCaMP8m imaging in dorsal CA1.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge the extensive validation, noting 'many published studies have relied on this system' and that the design 'has been validated by the myriad experimental paradigms that have been successfully implemented.' The experimental methods for the current study are accepted without critique.

result: The treadmill system design features a belt-based platform without support directly beneath the mouse to reduce vibrations, adjustable goniometers for head angle optimization, sliding frame for belt tension adjustment, and a lap-reset feature to prevent position tracking drift. Belts can be customized with various tactile cues.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the treadmill design as part of the overall system validation. One reviewer specifically mentions 'the computer vision-based calibration of treadmill' as an 'innovative approach.' The design features are not questioned or critiqued.

result: The VR system uses five monitors in an octagonal configuration (135° between displays) positioned to align with mouse visual field. Alternative tablet-based wireless configurations are available for space-constrained setups. The system supports hybrid setups combining visual and tactile cues, and custom shaders can filter specific colors to minimize imaging artifacts.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm the VR implementation, noting it 'relies on Unity, a common game development engine, but implements all scene generation and customizability in the authors' behaviorMate and VRMate software.' The flexibility and innovative features are praised without critique of the specific hardware configurations.

result: Head-restrained navigation systems address the challenge of studying neural circuits during behavior while enabling advanced imaging techniques. Spatial representations from freely moving animals (place cells, grid cells) are conserved in head-restrained VR and treadmill setups, validating these approaches for studying hippocampal and entorhinal cortex function.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these background claims as established context for the work. The manuscript's citations to prior literature supporting conservation of spatial representations in head-fixed setups are not questioned, and reviewers acknowledge the system addresses an important methodological need in the field.

result: Detailed methods for animal preparation, 2-photon imaging, calcium signal processing (Suite2p, OASIS), place cell classification, and Bayesian decoding analysis. All experiments followed NIH guidelines with Columbia University IACUC approval. Analysis used binarized event signals with specific thresholds and spatial binning parameters.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about the experimental methods or analysis approaches. The documentation is implicitly accepted as adequate, with one reviewer noting 'Documentation for installing and operating behaviorMate is available via the authors' lab website and Github.' The methods are treated as standard and appropriate for the field.

result: Other open-source behavioral control systems exist, but behaviorMate distinguishes itself by not requiring users to write code and using compiled Arduino programs to maximize performance without interpreter overhead.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this distinction, with one noting the 'Plug & Play feature requiring no coding experience' as an advantage. The comparison to other systems is accepted as a valid positioning of the contribution.
